description: The oracle for metalog_validate's self-test. Every expectation here is HAND-AUTHORED from SPEC.md and the shipped schemas, never captured from a run: an expectation copied out of the tool under test would make the tool its own oracle, and the pair would agree forever while both were wrong. The `control` tag on a fixture names the specific way this validator could have gone green while blind; metalog_validate refuses to run its self-test if any of them is missing from this file.
findings_encoding: [instance path, failing keyword, offending member names, error count, documents affected]
first_documents_encoding: one label per finding, in order: the document a finding was FIRST seen in. Under a pointer that selects every element of an array the label is the file name followed by the concrete RFC 6901 pointer of the element, e.g. `report.json/raw/2/diff`; otherwise it is the label the corpus reader already used. Optional in general and MANDATORY on any fixture whose pointer carries the every-element token — metalog_validate derives that demand from the pointer itself and refuses to run without it, because a count alone ('1 of 4') passes against a validator that judges every element and names the wrong one.
refusal_mentions_encoding: a substring the instrument's own message must contain. MANDATORY on any exit-2 fixture that carries a pointer, and derived from the fixture rather than listed here: exit 2 is a CLASS, not a reason, and a pointer refusal has several — the member is absent, the wire shape moved, the selection is empty, the walk hit a scalar. A fixture asserting only the number passes against an instrument that refuses for a reason nobody intended.

unadjudicated_directories.unarmed: Fixtures authored against a rule the shipped schemas cannot yet express, so wiring them would assert a verdict against a schema that cannot answer the question. They are kept in the repository, out of the adjudicated corpus, until the rule lands in SPEC.md and the schemas; metalog_validate refuses to run its self-test if this exemption carries no reason, and prints how many files it currently holds so an exemption that grows cannot grow quietly.

cap_violations_encoding: [instance path, cap field, value the document declares, actual array length, documents affected]

fixtures.why: the five required blocks and nothing else — the baseline a conformant producer must clear

exercises EVERY open container the schema opens on purpose — extensions (§7), source.tags, param_histogram.value_counts, cube coordinates keyed by axis name (§16.4), attribution.sketch_params (§6, a REQUIRED map whose keys depend on sketch_type) and provenance[].source (§12.4). All are described BY MECHANISM, so the undescribed walker must report zero. A walker that reports any of these would send a lane to delete a field the schema does describe. The last two carried NOTHING until 2026-08-24: this entry claimed "sketch-shaped free objects" while the document had no attribution block at all, so the two positions whose disposition the closure walk has to rule on were the two positions this control could not see. With them present, writing their openness down instead of leaving additionalProperties absent reds this fixture with five invented findings on a fully conformant document — unless the walker reads what an open declaration MEANS rather than whether the keyword is spelled out.

a member at the OPEN root and a second one nested inside provenance[].window, which is also open. Two locations on purpose: a root-only walker finds one of them and looks correct. Neither is a schema violation.

the closed-object defect class at two instance paths, one of them (cube.axes[]) reachable only by following a two-hop $ref chain — cube -> $defs/cube -> axes.items -> $defs/cube_axis — so a walker that stops at the first $ref reds here. Each object carries a LEGAL member beside the illegal one: `component` and `band_floor` are standard from v0.8.0 and MUST validate, while `vendor_private_counter` is vendor data written bare instead of into `extensions` (SPEC §7) and MUST NOT. Two rejected members on the top_k row prove the report lists EVERY offender, not just the first. `vendor_private_counter` is deliberately a name the standard can never mint: until v0.8.0 this fixture's violations WERE `component` and `band_floor`, and describing them in the schema silently disarmed it — teeth made out of a live defect fall out the day the defect is fixed.

two keywords that are NOT additionalProperties — a missing required member and a template_id that fails §3.2's pattern. Without this the report could be additionalProperties-shaped and nobody would notice.

THE green-BLIND antidote. Two `### name ###` sections, three documents, and the ONLY violation sits on the second line of the first section. A reader that treats a section as one document reports 2 documents and 0 findings — a smaller, entirely plausible, silently wrong result. Here that reader fails twice over: wrong document count AND a missed finding. The violating member is `vendor_private_counter`, a name the standard can never mint, and that choice is load-bearing: this control's subject is the READER, so it must never go quiet for a reason that has nothing to do with line-reading. It did exactly that once — the violation used to be `component`, and standardising `component` in v0.8.0 left the fixture parsing three documents and finding nothing, i.e. the antidote passing while testing the failure mode it exists to catch.
the second schema is a first-class subject, not an afterthought — a MetaLogDiff (§13) that conforms, read from a single-document .json file
proves the diff leg can FAIL too — an extra member inside `current`, which the diff schema closes

the v0.9.0 `run_outcome` adoption (SPEC §2.5), both directions in ONE corpus — two documents, because one document can carry only one value. Line 1 spells it `failure` and MUST validate AND MUST NOT be reported undescribed: describing the member is what takes it out of the open root's shadow. Line 2 spells it `SUCCESS` and MUST be rejected — the enum is closed and case-sensitive, and lower case is what this spec mints (`sketch_type`, `cube.axes[].kind`) as against `level`, whose tokens come from the observed stream. `SUCCESS` is not an invented mistake: it is exactly what the reference implementation emits today, so this fixture is the executable form of the divergence GOVERNANCE §3 resolves in the spec's favour. It is also the ONLY fixture in this set that exercises an `enum` violation at all — every other finding here is `additionalProperties`, `required` or `pattern`. Revert the adoption and it reds three ways: the finding disappears, the exit drops to 0, and `run_outcome` joins the undescribed list on BOTH documents.

the v0.9.0 `reservoir_delta` adoption (SPEC §13.7), with a legal sibling beside the illegal member so the report has to discriminate. The `new_salient` entry is fully conformant — required `template_id`/`count`/`salience` plus the two optional §3.7.1 members — and MUST validate; the `frontier_crossings` entry spells `direction` as `increased`, which the closed `up`/`down` enum MUST reject. Direction is the right member to put teeth in: it is the one place in this block where a plausible synonym changes meaning, and the enum is what stops a producer inventing `escalated`/`recovered` and shipping the polarity reading §13.7.2 refuses to make. Revert the adoption and this reds three ways — the finding disappears, the exit drops to 0, and `reservoir_delta` joins the undescribed list.

the v0.9.0 diff-root `extensions` grant (SPEC §7), proved in both directions inside ONE document. The container is now DESCRIBED, so its reverse-DNS grammar is enforced at this root: `topology_delta` written bare inside `extensions` is rejected, while `com.example.topology_delta` beside it MUST validate — a legal member next to the illegal one, so the report has to discriminate rather than reject the object wholesale. These teeth cannot fall out the way a fixture built on a live defect can: no future standardisation can make an unprefixed key legal INSIDE `extensions`, whatever the standard mints elsewhere. `vendor_private_counter` sits bare at the diff ROOT to hold the limit the grant does NOT close — that root is open, so the member is legal-but-undescribed and changes no exit code. Revert the grant and this fixture reds three ways: the finding disappears, the exit drops to 0, and `extensions` itself joins the undescribed list.

SPEC §8 clause 4 at two locations, in a document that is SCHEMA-VALID — which is the whole point: JSON Schema's `maxItems` takes a constant, the bound here is the value of a sibling field, so no schema-only test can reach this defect and a validator that only validates reports CONFORMANT on it. Two locations because a stats-only checker finds `top_k_size` and looks correct; `branching_size` is reached only by the schema-derived pair rule, so a hand-kept list that was never updated reds here. The vendor object under `extensions` carries `shard_size: 1` beside a three-element `shard` array on purpose: `extensions` is vendor space (§7) and this standard does not adjudicate it — a walker that reports three violations instead of two is claiming an authority it does not have.

a document carried INSIDE a larger envelope, the shape a CI report takes when it quotes the diff it was built from. Without this fixture the --pointer path ships untested, and an untested path in a gate is the never-ran failure mode one level down.

the same envelope with a pointer that does not resolve. Exit 2: a document the pointer cannot reach is a corpus this run cannot judge, never one it may quietly skip — a skipped file shrinks the corpus, which is the one thing this instrument must never do.

the SAME envelope as the two entries above, read with the every-element pointer — and `raw` here is a single OBJECT, the wire shape a report carried before its producer started publishing one diff per comparison. `-` is a wildcard only where an ARRAY sits; against an object RFC 6901 already gives it a meaning, a literal member name, and this instrument does not overrule RFC 6901 to be helpful. So the run REFUSES rather than judging the envelope as though it were a diff, and `refusal_mentions` pins WHICH refusal: a resolver that gave the token a second meaning would also exit 2, one token later, on a scalar it had no business reaching. That the coupling reds loudly is the point — repointing at the array without republishing the corpus must stop the run, not go quietly green over one element of a shape that no longer exists.

expect.refusal_mentions: RFC 6901 reads it as a literal member name

fixtures.why: an envelope with a member literally spelled `-`, beside a second member — and this is the fixture that keeps the extension from swallowing the standard it extends. RFC 6901 gives `-` a meaning in an ARRAY (the element after the last, which never exists, which is what makes the token free to mean `every element` here) and a different one in an OBJECT (a literal member name, which resolves perfectly well). An implementation that reads the token as a wildcard everywhere would select BOTH members here and judge two documents; the correct reading selects one — the invalid one, deliberately, so the assertion is not merely a count. `first_documents` pins the second half: a non-expanding pointer must leave the label the corpus reader already had, the FILE name with no pointer appended, which is exactly what every existing caller's output depends on.

THE anti-blindness fixture, and the shape a CI report actually takes: `raw` is a LIST with one {unit, diff} entry per comparison the producer performed. FOUR entries here; entry 2 (`package`) carries `vendor_private_counter` bare inside `current`, which the diff schema closes. Entries 0, 1 and 3 are fully conformant, and that ordering is the entire teeth: a validator whose pointer resolves to ONE document judges entry 0, finds nothing, and prints the same confident CONFORMANT over a corpus that contains a violation — subject-incomplete, not smaller. The contrast is pinned as the very next entry in this file: the same bytes under `/raw/0/diff` MUST read exit 0 over 1 document, so the two entries together are the executable form of the finding rather than a measurement somebody has to re-run. `documents: 4` is load-bearing beside the finding: a walker that judged all four but reported a count of one would still be lying about the subject. `vendor_private_counter` is a name the standard can never mint, so these teeth cannot fall out the day a member is standardised — the failure mode that silently disarmed two fixtures in this set once already.

THE CONTRAST, and it belongs in the manifest rather than in a report: the same four-entry envelope as the entry above, read with the naive repoint. Exit 0 over ONE document — a truthful sentence about entry 0 and a green over a corpus whose entry 2 is invalid. This entry is not a wish; it is the recorded behaviour a single-document pointer HAS, kept executable so that nobody re-derives it and so that the every-element entry above cannot be read as an improvement in degree. It doubles as the compatibility pin: an explicit numeric index still selects exactly one document and still names it by FILE, unchanged, which is what every existing caller of --pointer relies on.

the array is present, well-formed, and EMPTY — the shape a report takes when its producer performed no comparison, or when a refresh regressed to zero. The pointer resolves perfectly and selects nothing, so there is no unreadable byte anywhere to trip the instrument-failure control: this is the OTHER way a corpus reaches zero, and the only one an exception-shaped guard cannot see. Exit 2. A run that judged zero documents and printed CONFORMANT would be green for the one reason that matters, that it never looked — and unlike a missing file it would be green while every path it took was correct.

two every-element tokens in one pointer — the aggregate envelope, several runs each carrying several comparisons. The selection is the CARTESIAN set, 2 x 2 = 4 documents, and the only violation sits at runs[1].raw[1], reachable by neither a first-run-only nor a first-comparison-only reader. Without this entry the multi-token path would ship untested, which is the never-ran failure mode one level down from the one the entry above closes: the expansion is written as a loop over tokens, so a second token costs no branch of its own — and an untested loop is exactly where an off-by-one hides. `first_documents` pins the full concrete pointer, so a walker that judges all four and mislabels which one failed still reds here.

a truncated final line, the shape a crashed writer leaves. Must be exit 2 and never exit 0: a corpus the reader cannot fully read has no verdict, and skipping the bad line would report the remaining documents as clean.
a corpus file that exists and carries nothing. Zero documents is exit 2, never exit 0 — a gate with nothing to judge is green for the one reason that matters: it never looked.
